description: Day 06 benchmark over 11 PEPs. Written and split (15 dev / 5 test) BEFORE any retrieval run. gold_page = content-unit index inside the document (see data/manifest.json). Evidence quotes are verified against the normalized units by `python -m src.run validate`. Filters are user-context inputs (e.g. 'I am reading the Standards Track specification'), never the gold document id.
split_rule: Test questions cover documents/sections not used by any dev question where possible (PEP 8 naming, PEP 484 NewType/Any, PEP 483, mapping patterns). Leak risk: dev and test share PEP 8, PEP 484 and the pattern-matching PEPs, so retrieval behaviour on those documents is partially seen during dev.
selection_criteria_fixed_before_test: Pick the strategy with the highest dev Evidence Hit@3; tie-break on dev Hit@1, then manual grounding, then fewer chunks / lower ingest time.

questions.question: What is the maximum line length recommended for Python code in the style guide?
questions.expected_answer: 79 characters
questions.evidence_quote: Limit all lines to a maximum of 79 characters.

questions.question: If a team agrees on longer lines, how long may code lines be and what limit still applies to comments and docstrings?
questions.expected_answer: Up to 99 characters, as long as comments and docstrings are still wrapped at 72 characters
questions.evidence_quote: it is okay to increase the line length limit up to 99 characters, provided that comments and docstrings are still wrapped at 72 characters

questions.question: How many spaces should be used per indentation level?
questions.expected_answer: 4 spaces
questions.evidence_quote: Use 4 spaces per indentation level.

questions.question: When a long arithmetic expression wraps, should the newline come before or after the plus sign?
questions.expected_answer: Before the operator (mathematical tradition / Knuth style)
questions.evidence_quote: displayed formulas always break before binary operations

questions.question: Why is catching every exception with an empty except clause discouraged?
questions.expected_answer: A bare except: also catches SystemExit and KeyboardInterrupt, making Ctrl-C harder and hiding other problems
questions.evidence_quote: A bare except: clause will catch SystemExit and KeyboardInterrupt exceptions

questions.question: Should multiple modules be imported on one line like import sys, os?
questions.expected_answer: No, imports should usually be on separate lines
questions.evidence_quote: Imports should usually be on separate lines

questions.question: Why use triple quotes for a docstring that fits on a single line?
questions.expected_answer: It makes it easy to expand the docstring later
questions.evidence_quote: Triple quotes are used even though the string fits on one line. This makes it easy to later expand it.

questions.question: What does a Process PEP describe?
questions.expected_answer: A process surrounding Python, or a change to (or an event in) a process
questions.evidence_quote: A Process PEP describes a process surrounding Python, or proposes a change to (or an event in) a process.

questions.question: What must the authors do when none of the co-authors can act as sponsor for their proposal?
questions.expected_answer: The PEP author(s) must find a sponsor for the PEP
questions.evidence_quote: Otherwise (i.e. none of the co-authors are sponsors), the PEP author(s) will need to find a sponsor for the PEP.

questions.question: Which file extension do type stub files use and why?
questions.expected_answer: .pyi, so stubs can live in the same directory as the real module
questions.evidence_quote: they use the .pyi extension to make it possible to maintain stub files in the same directory as the corresponding real module

questions.question: What does annotating an attribute with ClassVar tell the static type checker?
questions.expected_answer: That the variable is a class variable and should not be set on instances
questions.evidence_quote: ClassVar is a special class defined by the typing module that indicates to the static type checker that this variable should not be set on instances

questions.question: Is it valid to write y := f(x) as a standalone statement without parentheses?
questions.expected_answer: No; unparenthesized assignment expressions are prohibited at the top level of an expression statement
questions.evidence_quote: Unparenthesized assignment expressions are prohibited at the top level of an expression statement.

questions.question: In the formal specification, what happens if evaluating a case guard raises an exception?
questions.expected_answer: The exception bubbles up
questions.evidence_quote: the expression in the guard is evaluated. If this raises an exception, the exception bubbles up.
questions.filter_context: User states they are reading the Standards Track (normative) documents.

questions.question: What does the __match_args__ attribute of a class do for pattern matching?
questions.expected_answer: It defines an explicit order of attributes so they can be matched positionally, e.g. case Click((x, y))
questions.evidence_quote: The __match_args__ special attribute defines an explicit order for your attributes

alt_gold.evidence_quote: You can also define a specific position for attributes in patterns by setting the __match_args__ special attribute in your classes.
The class field __match_args__ specifies a number of attributes together with their ordering, allowing class patterns to rely on positional sub-patterns

questions.filter_context: User asks for explanatory (Informational) material, not the normative spec.

questions.question: How should a value be compared with None?
questions.expected_answer: With is or is not, never with equality operators
questions.evidence_quote: Comparisons to singletons like None should always be done with is or is not, never the equality operators.
questions.filter_context: User asks for the process/style-guide recommendation (Process documents).

questions.question: What naming style should class names normally follow?
questions.expected_answer: CapWords
questions.evidence_quote: Class names should normally use the CapWords convention.

questions.question: How do I declare a distinct UserId type built on int so the type checker treats it as separate from plain int?
questions.expected_answer: UserId = NewType('UserId', int)
questions.evidence_quote: UserId = NewType('UserId', int)

alt_gold.evidence_quote: NewType, used to create unique types with little runtime overhead UserId = NewType('UserId', int)

questions.question: Which new relation does gradual typing introduce that behaves like subtyping but is not transitive when Any is involved?
questions.expected_answer: is-consistent-with
questions.evidence_quote: We define a new relationship, is-consistent-with, which is similar to is-subtype-of, except it is not transitive when the new type Any is involved.

questions.question: Does a mapping pattern still match if the dictionary has additional keys?
questions.expected_answer: Yes, extra keys are ignored (unless captured with **rest)
questions.evidence_quote: extra keys in the subject will be ignored while matching

alt_gold.evidence_quote: Unlike sequence patterns, extra keys are ignored.
Extra keys in the subject are ignored even if **rest is not present.

questions.filter_context: User asks for explanatory (Informational) material, not the normative spec.

questions.question: Which special type is every type consistent with?
questions.expected_answer: Any
questions.evidence_quote: A special kind of type is Any. Every type is consistent with Any.
questions.filter_context: User states they are reading the Standards Track (normative) documents.
